name: Literature Review Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday literature review work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical literature review tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday literature review work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical literature review tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep literature review changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen literature review approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. State assumptions about literature review explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Measure before optimizing any literature review bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. When literature review guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Check that literature review terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. Document any non-obvious literature review decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Before starting literature review work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to literature review (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
10. Prefer explicit, readable literature review solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
11. Keep literature review outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
12. Validate literature review outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic literature review advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated literature review concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of literature review correctness.
- Avoid introducing new literature review abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for literature review, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
